title: Test: Subject–Verb Agreement
subtitle: Answer all 10 detective questions to check your mastery of Subject–Verb Agreement. You can review every answer before submitting.

questions.questionText: Check this school orchard notice: 'The basket of fresh green mangoes _____ ready for the morning assembly.' Which verb matches the true Subject?
questions.explanation: Ignore the intervening phrase 'of fresh green mangoes'. The true Subject head-noun is singular 'basket', so the verb is singular 'is'.

questions.questionText: Read the mid-day meal poster: 'Rice and dal _____ served hot as a wholesome meal every afternoon.' Choose the accurate verb.
questions.explanation: 'Rice and dal' here expresses ONE combined dish ('a wholesome meal'), so it takes a singular verb ('is').

questions.questionText: Compare the determiners carefully: 'The Secretary and Headmaster _____ presiding over today's prize distribution.' Which verb fits?
questions.explanation: There is only ONE 'The' ('The Secretary and Headmaster'), meaning one person holds both roles, so singular 'is' is required.
questions.learningObjective: One vs two determiners in compound titles

questions.questionText: Complete the sports log: 'The captain, as well as the twelve players, _____ arrived on the ground.'
questions.explanation: When subjects are joined by 'as well as' or 'with', the verb agrees with the FIRST Subject ('The captain' → singular 'has').
questions.learningObjective: Concord with 'with / as well as' vs 'neither...nor'

questions.questionText: Choose the verb that agrees with the nearer subject: 'Neither Mira nor her classmates _____ visited the science museum yet.'
questions.explanation: With 'neither...nor' and 'either...or', the verb locks onto the NEARER subject ('her classmates', plural), taking plural 'have'.

questions.questionText: Which formal school notice follows standard subject–verb agreement for 'neither of'?

options.text: Neither of the two answers are clear enough.
Neither of the two answers is clear enough.
Neither of the two answers were clear enough.
Neither of the two answers have been clear.

questions.explanation: In formal grammar, 'neither of / each of / one of + plural noun' takes a singular verb ('is'). (Plural verbs sometimes appear in casual speech, but standard formal grammar expects singular.)

questions.questionText: Inspect these four sentences about '-s' nouns and always-plural nouns. Which one is completely accurate?

options.text: Mathematics are my sister's favourite subject.
The latest news from the ISRO centre are exciting.
The cattle was grazing near the river bank.
A pair of sharp scissors is lying on the craft desk.

questions.explanation: 'A pair of scissors' refers to one pair, so it takes singular 'is'. 'Mathematics' and 'news' are singular ('is'), whereas 'cattle' is plural ('were').

questions.questionText: In a preparatory 'There' sentence, look after the verb for the real Subject: 'There _____ forty wooden desks in Room 4.'
questions.explanation: In 'There...' sentences, the real Subject follows the verb. Because 'forty wooden desks' is plural, use plural 'are'.
questions.learningObjective: Matching verb to true Subject number and person

questions.questionText: Complete the sports day record: 'Five kilometres _____ a brisk morning walk for our trekking team.'
questions.explanation: Distances, sums of money, and weights seen as ONE single unit ('a brisk morning walk') take a singular verb ('is').
questions.learningObjective: Unit quantities treated as one whole

questions.questionText: Diagnose the agreement error in this classroom slip: 'Every student in both sections have submitted the science notebook.'

options.text: 'Every student' is singular, so 'have' must change to singular 'has'.

questions.explanation: Subjects beginning with 'Every' or 'Each' always act as singular, ignoring 'in both sections'; thus 'have' must be corrected to 'has'.
questions.learningObjective: Diagnosing and explaining Subject–Verb Agreement errors
